Activities show UI, Services do background work, an Intent is the message itself. Flutter: listen to plugin Streams (connectivity, battery) or your own broadcast StreamController (Module 3).

questionsList.content: Which component handle background processing associated with an application?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: Services handle background processing without a UI. Activities are screens, broadcast receivers react to events, content providers share data. Flutter (Module 3 – 'Use Isolates for heavy CPU tasks'): Futures/async for I/O, Isolates for CPU-heavy work; jobs that must survive app closure need workmanager/background-service plugins or native code.

questionsList.content: Which of the following are parts of a content URI?

answersList.content: The symbolic name of the provider
A name that points to a table or file
An optional part that points to an individual row in a table
Metadata defining the synchronization policy for concurrent access

questionsList.explanation: Correct: a content URI = content:// scheme + authority (the symbolic name of the provider) + path (points to a table or file) + an optional ID (points to an individual row). It contains no synchronization metadata. Flutter (Module 8): Dart's Uri class parses any URI — Uri.parse('content://com.example.provider/todos/5') exposes scheme, host (authority) and pathSegments.

questionsList.content: Choose the correct statement about key components of the System.Net.* Namespaces

answersList.content: A WebClient facade class for simple download/upload operations via HTTP or FTP
WebRequest and WebResponse classes for high-level control over client-side TCP or UDP operations
HttpServer for consuming HTTP web APIs and RESTful services

questionsList.explanation: Correct: WebClient is a facade class for simple download/upload operations via HTTP or FTP. WebRequest/WebResponse give low-level control over client-side HTTP/FTP (not TCP/UDP), HttpClient (not 'HttpServer') consumes HTTP web APIs, and HttpListener is used to write an HTTP server — so 'All of the others' is wrong. C#, outside the Flutter syllabus. Dart (Module 8): the http package (http.get/post) is the simple facade; dart:io HttpClient gives lower-level control.

questionsList.content: Which importance level of notification will make a sound when it appears?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: High and Urgent importance levels make a sound (Urgent also appears as a heads-up popup); Medium makes no sound, Low makes no sound and does not appear in the status bar. In code, IMPORTANCE_HIGH = 'Urgent' and IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT = 'High'. Flutter (Module 10): AndroidNotificationDetails(..., importance: Importance.high, priority: Priority.high) gives a heads-up with sound; Importance.defaultImportance plays a sound without the heads-up.

questionsList.content: Assume you have a TextView with a textSize attribute of 16sp. This TextView also has a style applied to it which sets textSize to 14sp. In addition, there is also a theme in the app that sets textSize to 12sp. What is the actual textSize of the TextView that will be displayed on screen?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: 16sp — an attribute set directly on the view overrides the style, which overrides the theme (view attribute > style > theme). Flutter (Module 4 – Theme): Text('x', style: const TextStyle(fontSize: 16)) wins over DefaultTextStyle and Theme.of(context).textTheme — a local style overrides the inherited theme.

questionsList.content: How do you send data from an activity to a fragment?

answersList.content: Set a Bundle and use the Fragment.setArguments(Bundle) method to supply the construction arguments for the fragment.
Use the Fragment method getArguments() to get the arguments.
Define an interface in the Fragment class, and implement the interface in the activity.
Call addToBackStack() during a transaction that removes the fragment.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: put the data in a Bundle and call fragment.setArguments(bundle) before adding the fragment; inside the fragment read it with getArguments(). Defining an interface in the Fragment is for fragment → activity communication, and addToBackStack() is unrelated. Flutter (Module 8 – Demo 8.2): pass data through the widget's constructor, e.g. PostDetailScreen(post: post), or through route arguments.

questionsList.content: What is the name of the file in which you create options menu items?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: menu_main.xml in res/menu, inflated in onCreateOptionsMenu(). activity_main.xml and content_main.xml are layouts, and menus are not defined in .java files. Flutter: menus are widgets — AppBar(actions: [IconButton(...), PopupMenuButton<String>(itemBuilder: ...)]) — no XML file.

questionsList.content: To display text which control will you use?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: TextView displays (read-only) text; EditText is for input, and Label/TextArea are not Android widgets. Flutter (Module 4): Text('Hello', style: const TextStyle(fontSize: 28)).

questionsList.content: Is a View also known as a Widget in Android?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: True — in Android, View subclasses such as Button and TextView are commonly called widgets (they live in the android.widget package). Flutter (Module 1/4): 'Everything is a Widget' — every screen, button and text is a widget.

questionsList.content: FragmentManager is the class responsible for performing actions on your app's fragments, such as adding, removing, or replacing them, and adding them to the back stack.
questionsList.explanation: Correct: True — FragmentManager performs fragment transactions (add, remove, replace) and manages the fragment back stack. Flutter (Module 5): the Navigator manages the stack of routes (push, pop, pushReplacement).

questionsList.content: Which component do we use to open an URL in Android application?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: an implicit Intent — new Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse(url)) lets the system pick a browser. Explicit intents target your own classes; content providers and services are unrelated. Flutter: url_launcher — await launchUrl(Uri.parse('https://flutter.dev')); inside your own app, deep links map URLs to screens (Module 5).

questionsList.content: Which buttons does the Basic Activity template provide as part of the UI?

answersList.content: Button class button with the text "Button"

questionsList.explanation: [KEY CORRECTED] The original key marked only 'Floating action button'. The Basic Activity template provides both an app bar with an options-menu overflow button (menu_main.xml with a 'Settings' item) and a FloatingActionButton, so the correct choices are 'Options menu overflow button' and 'Floating action button'. If your exam accepts only one answer, choose 'Floating action button'. Flutter (Module 4 – Scaffold): Scaffold(appBar: AppBar(actions: [PopupMenuButton(...)]), floatingActionButton: FloatingActionButton(onPressed: () {}, child: const Icon(Icons.add))).

questionsList.content: Which of the following don't have any UI component and run as a background process?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: services have no UI and run in the background. An emulator/simulator is a development tool and an Intent is a message. Flutter: there is no UI-less component — background logic lives in Dart classes (services/repositories), Isolates, or native background plugins (Module 1, Module 3).

questionsList.content: What is the name of the layout file for the main activity?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: activity_main.xml (in res/layout) is the main activity's layout; MainActivity.java is code, AndroidManifest.xml is configuration, build.gradle is build configuration. Flutter (Module 1 – Project Structure): there is no layout file — UI is written in Dart in lib/main.dart (the entry point) and other files under lib/.

questionsList.content: How does RecyclerView display items?

answersList.content: It displays items in a list or a grid.
It scrolls diagonally on larger devices, such as tablets.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: RecyclerView displays items in a list or a grid, scrolls vertically or horizontally, and supports custom layouts (custom item layouts / LayoutManagers). It does not scroll diagonally. Flutter (Module 4/6): ListView (scrollDirection: Axis.horizontal or vertical), GridView, and fully custom item widgets.

questionsList.content: Which of the following correctly describe what is meant by an Intent being a "passive" data structure?

answersList.content: An intent just consists of fields and field access/mutator methods
An intent cannot be used in a concurrent program
An intent only contains public fields
An intent only contains static getter/setter methods

questionsList.explanation: Correct: 'passive' means an Intent just consists of fields (action, data, extras...) and accessor/mutator (getter/setter) methods — it does not do any work itself; the system acts on it. It can be used in concurrent programs and does not have only public fields or static methods. Flutter (Module 8): route arguments and model objects such as Post (final fields only) are similar passive data carriers.

questionsList.content: Which of the following are reasons why Android apps typically use concurrency or asynchrony when accessing an SQLite database?

answersList.content: Filesystem accesses are often relatively slow
SQLite supports the SQL92 specification, which is obsolete
Android filesystems are unreliable due to their use of flash memory

questionsList.explanation: Correct: file-system access (flash storage) is relatively slow, so database work should run asynchronously to avoid freezing the UI. SQLite does support synchronous operations, and SQL92 or flash reliability are not the reasons. Flutter (Module 9 notes): sqflite operations are async — always await db.query() etc. — so the UI isolate is not blocked.

questionsList.content: Which pair of methods do you use to register and unregister your broadcast receiver dynamically?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: registerReceiver() and unregisterReceiver() (typically in onStart/onStop or onResume/onPause). The other method pairs do not exist for receivers. Flutter (Module 2 – 'Subscribe with listen, cancel with subscription.cancel()'): final sub = stream.listen(...) in initState() and sub.cancel() in dispose().

questionsList.content: Which API do you use to show a notification in the notification drawer and in the device's status bar?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: NotificationManager.notify() (or NotificationManagerCompat.notify()) shows the notification in the notification drawer and status bar; NotificationCompat.Builder only builds the Notification object. Flutter (Module 10): FlutterLocalNotificationsPlugin().show(id, title, body, const NotificationDetails(android: AndroidNotificationDetails('channel_id', 'Channel name'))).

questionsList.content: Which XML attribute do you use in a LinearLayout to show views side by side?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: android:orientation="horizontal" places the children side by side; vertical stacks them. Flutter (Module 4/5): Row(children: [...]) is horizontal and Column is vertical.

questionsList.content: How to store heavy structured data in android?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: an SQLite database is used for heavy/large structured data. SharedPreferences is only for small key–value data, and a Cursor is just a pointer over query results. Flutter (Module 9 – When to use which storage): 'Large structured data → SQLite (SQFlite)'.

questionsList.content: Which of the following statements accurately reflect what happens when a user enters text via the Android virtual keyboard?

answersList.content: The onStart() hook method is called back and the activity becomes visible
The onResume() hook method is called back to return UI focus for this screen
The UI focus is unchanged and no lifecycle hook methods are called
A new activity is started and its onCreate() hook method is called

questionsList.explanation: Correct: typing on the virtual keyboard does not change UI focus or trigger any lifecycle callback — the activity stays resumed (the window may only resize). No new activity starts. Flutter (Module 7): the keyboard changes MediaQuery.viewInsets.bottom and the Scaffold may resize and rebuild, but no lifecycle event occurs; wrap forms in a ListView / SingleChildScrollView to avoid overflow.

questionsList.content: Which component should we use to share the data across all applications?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: a Content Provider is the component designed to share data with other applications (through content URIs and permissions). SharedPreferences, internal storage and SQLite databases are private to the app. Flutter: there is no Dart equivalent for app-to-app data sharing; use share_plus (share text/files via intents) or native code via Platform Channels; within the app use SharedPreferences/SQLite (Module 9).

questionsList.content: Assume that your app includes this logging statement: Log.i("MainActivity", "MainActivity layout is complete"); You see the statement "MainActivity layout is complete" in the Logcat panel. Which of the following log level menu is set?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: Verbose, Debug and Info — Logcat shows messages at the selected level and above, so an Info message (Log.i) appears when the filter is Verbose, Debug or Info, but not when it is Warn or Error. Flutter (Module 11): print() / debugPrint() output appears in Logcat and the debug console; dart:developer log() supports levels and appears in DevTools Logging.

questionsList.content: Which is the file that contains all the text that an Android application uses?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: strings.xml (res/values/strings.xml) contains the app's text resources and enables localization. Flutter: text lives in Dart (constants) or, for localization, in ARB files with flutter_localizations / intl (not covered in the slides).

questionsList.content: Which of the following are Android RecyclerView layout managers?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: GridLayoutManager and LinearLayoutManager (StaggeredGridLayoutManager is the third built-in one). RecyclingManager and CircularLayoutManager do not exist. Flutter (Module 4/6): ListView.builder and GridView.count / GridView.builder.

questionsList.content: How do you add a query option to a REST web-service call in Retrofit?

answersList.content: Append the query to the end of the request URL.
Add a parameter for the query to the function that makes the request and annotate the parameter with @Query.
Use the Query class to build a request.
Use the addQuery() method in the Retrofit builder.

questionsList.explanation: Correct (key): append the query to the end of the request URL, or — the idiomatic Retrofit way — add a function parameter annotated with @Query. [CHECK] The original Google codelab answer is only the @Query option; if your exam is single-choice, choose @Query. There is no Query class or addQuery() builder method. Flutter (Module 8): Uri.https('api.example.com', '/movies', {'sort': 'name'}) or Uri.parse(url).replace(queryParameters: {...}).

questionsList.content: Which kernel is Android based on?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: Android is based on the Linux kernel (drivers, memory, process and power management). Flutter (Module 1 – Architecture): Flutter has its own three layers — Framework (Dart) → Engine (C++) → Embedder (platform-specific, e.g. the Android embedder running on that Linux-based OS).

questionsList.content: In order to open screenB from screenA and receive data from screenB, which sentence should we use?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: startActivityForResult() (today the Activity Result API, registerForActivityResult) opens screen B and receives its result in onActivityResult(). startActivity() cannot return data; startActivities() starts several; startActivityResult() does not exist. Flutter (Module 5 + Module 9 dialog demo): final result = await Navigator.push(context, MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => const ScreenB())); and in B: Navigator.pop(context, data); — the same pattern as showDialog returning Navigator.pop(context, text).

questionsList.content: Which permission should Android app use when the app wants to track phone's precise location?
questionsList.explanation: [KEY CORRECTED] The original key marked both ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION and ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION. Tracking the phone's PRECISE location requires android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION; ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION only gives an approximate location (about city-block level). (On Android 12+ you request FINE together with COARSE and the user may still grant only approximate.) ACCESS_LOCATION does not exist and INTERNET is unrelated. Flutter: declare ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION in AndroidManifest.xml and use geolocator — await Geolocator.requestPermission(); await Geolocator.getCurrentPosition(locationSettings: const LocationSettings(accuracy: LocationAccuracy.high));

questionsList.content: What are the advantages of using a Room database?

answersList.content: Creates and manages an Android SQLite database for you.
Eliminates a lot of boilerplate code.
Using a DAO, provides a mechanism for mapping Java methods to database queries.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: Room creates and manages the SQLite database for you, eliminates a lot of boilerplate (no manual Cursor handling), and maps DAO methods to SQL queries with compile-time checks. It does not manage multiple applications. Flutter (Module 9): sqflite is closer to raw SQLite; Drift / Floor add Room-like code generation.

questionsList.content: Select all that are true for notification channels

answersList.content: You use notification channels to display notifications to the user in the device status bar.
You use notification channels to group multiple notifications so that the user can control the notifications' behavior.
Notification channels are available in older devices, those running Android 7.0 Nougat (API 24) and lower.
Notification channels are not yet available in the Android Support Library package.

questionsList.explanation: [KEY CORRECTED] The original key marked options 1 and 2 (votes split 11/20). Following the Android Developer Fundamentals answer: (2) channels group multiple notifications so the user can control their behavior, and (4) notification channels were not available in the Support Library at that time (NotificationChannel exists only in the API 26+ framework). Option 1 is false — NotificationManager displays notifications, a channel only categorizes them; option 3 is false — channels exist only on Android 8.0 (API 26)+. Note: AndroidX Core now has NotificationChannelCompat, so statement 4 is outdated today. Flutter (Module 10): AndroidNotificationChannel in flutter_local_notifications is simply ignored on Android < 8.

questionsList.content: Which of the following are true statements about Java threads?

answersList.content: A thread is the smallest unit of execution for sequences of programmed instructions
A Java thread must be given code to run when it is started
Starting a thread takes a trivial amount of time and system resources
Starting a Java thread is the only way to write a concurrent Android app

questionsList.explanation: Correct: (1) a thread is the smallest unit of execution for a sequence of programmed instructions and (2) a Java thread must be given code to run (a Runnable or an overridden run()). Starting a thread is NOT cheap in time/resources, and threads are not the only way to write concurrent Android apps (executors, coroutines, WorkManager...). Flutter (Module 3): Dart uses isolates (own memory + event loop) instead of shared-memory threads; async/await gives concurrency on a single isolate.

questionsList.content: Which command should we use to clear all data in a SharedPreference?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: clear() — editor.clear().apply() (or commit()) removes all values; remove(key) deletes a single key; delete()/destroy() do not exist. Flutter (Module 9): await prefs.clear(); removes all keys, await prefs.remove('auth_token'); removes one (used for logout in Module 10 Demo 10.3).

questionsList.content: What is difference between android api and google api?

answersList.content: The google API includes Google Maps and other Google-specific libraries. The Android one only includes core android libraries.
The google API one only includes core android libraries. The Android includes Google Maps and other Google-specific libraries.
The android API includes Google Maps and core android libraries. The google API includes Google libraries
The android API and Google API is same

questionsList.explanation: Correct: the Google APIs add-on includes Google Maps and other Google-specific libraries (Play services), while the plain Android API only includes the core Android libraries. Flutter (Module 10 – 'Emulator lacks Google Play Services'): use an emulator image 'with Google Play' for Google Sign-In / Maps.

questionsList.content: What does an Intent's action represent in Android?

answersList.content: The name of the component to be started
The type of operation to be performed, such as "ACTION_VIEW," "ACTION_SEND", "ACTION_DIAL"
The layout of the user interface
The permissions required to use the Intent.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: the action is a string naming the type of operation to perform, e.g. ACTION_VIEW, ACTION_SEND, ACTION_DIAL. The component name, layout and permissions are separate concepts. Flutter (Module 5): the deep-link intent-filter uses <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW"/>; url_launcher fires ACTION_VIEW (https:) or ACTION_DIAL (tel:) for you.

questionsList.content: Which of the following are true statements about the Android apps?

answersList.content: The bulk of these apps are written in C/C++
The bulk of these apps are written in Java
It's possible to write portions of the apps in C/C++
These apps cannot be written in C/C++

questionsList.explanation: Correct: the bulk of Android apps are written in Java (and today Kotlin, Google's preferred language), and portions can be written in C/C++ through the NDK/JNI. Flutter (Module 1): Flutter apps are written in Dart; native parts in Kotlin/Java (Android) or Swift (iOS) via Platform Channels; Dart FFI can call C/C++.

questionsList.content: Which of the following are Jetpack libraries that could be used in the data layer?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: Room is the Jetpack library for the data layer (DataStore too, but it is not listed). ViewModel belongs to the UI layer, Navigation to UI navigation, and 'Data' is not a library. Flutter (Module 3/9): the data layer = repositories + data sources such as sqflite, shared_preferences and an http ApiService.

questionsList.content: What is broadcast receiver in android?

answersList.content: It will react on broadcast announcements.
It will do background functionalities as services.
It will pass the data between activities

questionsList.explanation: Correct: a broadcast receiver reacts to broadcast announcements (from the system or other apps). It does not do background work like a service or pass data between activities. Flutter: Stream listeners react to events (Module 3).

questionsList.content: What is mean by ANR?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: ANR = Application Not Responding — the dialog shown when the main thread is blocked too long (about 5 seconds for input events). Flutter (Module 3/12): blocking the main isolate (heavy loops, synchronous parsing in build()) freezes frames (jank) and makes the app feel unresponsive; use async I/O and Isolates.

questionsList.content: Which of the following is not a layer in Android Architecture?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: 'Android Real Time' is not a layer — the real component is the Android Runtime (ART). The layers are Linux kernel, HAL, native Libraries + Android Runtime, Application Framework and Applications. Flutter (Module 1): Flutter's own architecture layers are Framework (Dart), Engine (C++) and Embedder.

questionsList.content: Which component contains fragments?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: an Activity hosts (contains) fragments. Flutter: a screen (a route widget, usually a Scaffold) contains child widgets; nested Navigators can host sub-flows.

questionsList.content: Which layout has android:layout_alignParentTop attribute?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: android:layout_alignParentTop is a RelativeLayout layout parameter. Flutter (Module 5 – Hero banner): Stack with Positioned(top: 0, ...) or Align(alignment: Alignment.topCenter, ...).

questionsList.content: Which of followings are components in MVVM architecture?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: Model, View and ViewModel; Presenter belongs to MVP. Flutter (Module 5/11): Model (Task), View (widgets), ViewModel (a ChangeNotifier provider such as TaskProvider).

questionsList.content: Which of the following statements sets the title for an alert dialog?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: myAlertBuilder.setTitle("Alert"); — setMessage() sets the body, setPositiveButton() needs a label and a listener, and the Builder constructor takes a Context, not a title. Flutter (Module 9 demos): showDialog(context: context, builder: (_) => AlertDialog(title: const Text('New Task'), content: ..., actions: [...])).

questionsList.content: The Room persistence library provides an abstraction layer to store the data easily. Where does the ROOM library store data?What is true about Fragments ?

answersList.content: A fragment has its own layout and its own behaviour with its own life cycle callbacks.
You can add or remove fragments in an activity while the activity is running.
You can combine multiple fragments in a single activity to build a multi-pane UI.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: All of the others — a fragment has its own layout, behavior and lifecycle callbacks; you can add or remove fragments while the activity is running; and you can combine several fragments in one activity to build a multi-pane UI. [CHECK] The question text is corrupted: it merges a Room question ('Where does Room store data?' — answer: in a local SQLite database on the device) with a Fragment question; the options answer the Fragment part. Flutter (Module 6 – Lab 6.3): a multi-pane UI = LayoutBuilder choosing a Row with a sidebar + content on wide screens.

questionsList.content: Which subclass of Fragment displays a vertical list of items that are managed by an adapter?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: ListFragment displays a vertical list of items managed by an adapter (ListAdapter). PreferenceFragment shows settings, DialogFragment dialogs, RowsFragment belongs to Leanback (TV). Flutter (Module 4): ListView.builder / ListView.separated with ListTile items.

questionsList.content: When is activity paused?

answersList.content: If activity is at background and still visible
If the activity is at foreground and visible
If the activity is at foreground

questionsList.explanation: Correct: an activity is paused when it is in the background but still visible — it lost focus because something partially covers it (a dialog-styled activity, multi-window). Not visible = stopped; foreground = resumed. Flutter: AppLifecycleState.inactive (visible but not receiving input) is the closest state; paused means not visible.

questionsList.content: Which of the following is a valid XML Document?
questionsList.explanation: Correct (key): option 1. [CHECK] As transcribed, none of the four options is valid XML: XML is case-sensitive so start and end tags must match exactly (<Order>…</Order>, <Customer>…</Customer>, <Orders>…</Orders>), attribute values must be quoted (Id="001"), and '&' must be escaped as &. The intended valid document is <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><Orders><Order Id="001"><Customer>David & Jason</Customer></Order></Orders>. Flutter (Module 8): REST APIs in the course use JSON, which is lighter; jsonDecode() parses it.

questionsList.content: Which component is changed significantly from Android 6.0?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: Permission — Android 6.0 (API 23) introduced runtime permissions: dangerous permissions are requested while the app runs and can be revoked by the user. Flutter: request at runtime with permission_handler or the plugin's own API; on Android 13+ notifications also need the runtime POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission (Module 10).

questionsList.content: What is NOT an activity lifetime?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: 'Background lifetime' is not an activity lifetime. The three lifetimes are the entire lifetime (onCreate → onDestroy), the visible lifetime (onStart → onStop) and the foreground lifetime (onResume → onPause). Flutter: a State object lives from initState() to dispose(); app visibility is reported by AppLifecycleState.

questionsList.content: Which of the following correctly describe what a broadcast receiver is in Android

answersList.content: An event handler that responds to broadcast announcements
A component that runs in the background to perform long-running operations or access remote resources
A component that defines a user-facing operation that's displayed on a device screen
A message that describes an action to perform or an event that has occurred

questionsList.explanation: Correct: a broadcast receiver is an event handler that responds to broadcast announcements. Option 2 describes a Service, option 3 an Activity, option 4 an Intent. Flutter: Stream listeners (Module 3).

questionsList.content: Which method of the socket module allows a server socket to accept requests from a client socket from another host?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: socket.accept() (Python socket module) accepts a connection on a listening server socket and returns (conn, address); the other names do not exist. Outside the Flutter syllabus. Dart: final server = await ServerSocket.bind(InternetAddress.anyIPv4, 4040); await for (final client in server) { ... } — each client is an accepted connection.

questionsList.content: Select a component which is NOT part of Android architecture
questionsList.explanation: Correct: 'Android document' is not part of the Android platform architecture, whereas the Android Framework, Libraries and Linux Kernel are layers of it. Flutter (Module 1): Flutter's architecture = Framework, Engine, Embedder.

questionsList.content: What is logcat window in android studio?

answersList.content: Log message is used to debug a program

questionsList.explanation: Correct: the Logcat window shows system and app log messages (Log.v/d/i/w/e), used to debug a program. It is not the same as printf() or a Toast shown to the user. Flutter (Module 11/12): print() / debugPrint() output appears in Logcat and the Run console; DevTools adds Logging, Inspector and Performance views.

questionsList.content: Which of the following are true statements about implicit and explicit intent?

answersList.content: Android delivers an explicit intent to a target component without consulting filters in the AndroidManifest.xml file
Implicit intents are typically used to interact with components residing in other apps
Explicit intents are typically used to interact with components residing in other apps
Android delivers an implicit intent to a target component only if it matches one of its intent filters in the AndroidManifest.xml file

questionsList.explanation: Correct: (1) Android delivers an explicit intent directly to the named component without consulting intent filters, (2) implicit intents are typically used to interact with components in other apps, and (4) an implicit intent is delivered only if it matches one of the component's intent filters. Explicit intents are mostly used inside your own app, so option 3 is false. Flutter (Module 5): Navigator.push (explicit, in-app) vs deep-link intent filters (implicit, from outside the app).

questionsList.content: What is the primary purpose of a Content Provider in Android?

answersList.content: To manage and share data between applications

questionsList.explanation: Correct: a Content Provider manages access to a structured set of data and shares it between applications. Network requests, background tasks and UI rendering belong to other components. Flutter: there is no ContentProvider in Dart; data sharing with other apps goes through plugins/native code, and the local data layer is a repository + SQLite (Module 9).

questionsList.content: The difference between SQLite and Content provider is:

answersList.content: Content provider is not a local database and SQLite is a local database.
Content provider is faster that SQLite.
Content provider can share data with other application but SQLite cannot.
SQLite can share data with other application but content provider cannot

questionsList.explanation: Correct: a content provider can share data with other applications (through URIs and permissions), while an SQLite database is private to the app that created it. A provider is not necessarily faster, and it may itself be backed by SQLite, files or the network. Flutter (Module 9): sqflite database files are private to the app.

questionsList.content: Which URI format is commonly used to access data from a Content Provider?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: content://authority/path/id — the standard content URI format; http://, provider:// and database:// are not used for Content Providers. Flutter (Module 8): Uri.parse() can parse it; http(s) URIs are used for the REST endpoints in the course.

questionsList.content: What method is used to send a broadcast event?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: sendBroadcast(intent); — startBroadcast, registerBroadcast and sendBroadcastReceiver do not exist. Flutter (Module 3): controller.add(event) on a StreamController.broadcast() delivers an event to all listeners inside the app.

questionsList.content: Which method is used to create a server socket in Android?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: new ServerSocket(PORT) (java.net) creates a server socket bound to the port; you then call accept(). ServerSocket.create() and SocketServer do not exist. Dart (dart:io, not in the slides): final server = await ServerSocket.bind(InternetAddress.anyIPv4, port);

questionsList.content: To add a button to a layout, which XML tag do you use in the layout file?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: <Button .../> — ImageButton shows an image instead of text, and InputButton/SubmitButton do not exist. Flutter (Module 4): ElevatedButton(onPressed: ..., child: const Text('Pick Date')), TextButton, OutlinedButton, IconButton.

questionsList.content: Which location in your project would you specify a pre-defined Theme (e.g., Theme.AppCompat.Light.DarkActionBar) to apply it to your application?

answersList.content: In the MainActivity.java (or Kotlin equivalent) file.
In the AndroidManifest.xml file within the <application> tag.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: in AndroidManifest.xml, with android:theme on the <application> tag (or on an individual <activity>); styles.xml only defines styles/themes, and layouts or Java code are not where the app-wide theme is applied. Flutter (Module 4): MaterialApp(theme: ..., darkTheme: ..., themeMode: ...) applies the theme to the whole app (the LaunchTheme/NormalTheme in the Flutter manifest only style the native splash window).

questionsList.content: Which ViewGroup would be most suitable to create a layout with two buttons side-by-side?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: LinearLayout (horizontal orientation) is the simplest ViewGroup for two buttons side by side; RelativeLayout/ConstraintLayout can do it but are more complex, and FrameLayout stacks children on top of each other. Flutter (Module 5 Step 4): Row(mainAxisAlignment: MainAxisAlignment.spaceEvenly, children: [button1, button2]); wrap each in Expanded for equal widths.

questionsList.content: Which method is most efficient for adding a fragment dynamically to an activity?
questionsList.explanation: Correct (key): beginTransaction() — getSupportFragmentManager().beginTransaction().add(R.id.container, fragment).commit(); every dynamic add/replace/remove starts with a FragmentTransaction. addFragment()/commitFragment() do not exist and addToBackStack() only records the transaction. Flutter (Module 5): screens are added dynamically with Navigator.push(); sub-widgets appear by changing state (setState / Provider).

questionsList.content: How does a Fragment differ from an Activity?

answersList.content: Fragments cannot exist without an Activity
Fragments do not have a lifecycle
Fragments are used for background processing
Activities are used to define UI

questionsList.explanation: Correct: fragments cannot exist without an Activity — a fragment must be hosted by an activity (or another fragment). Fragments do have a lifecycle, are UI components (not background workers), and both can define UI. Flutter: every widget lives in the tree under runApp() / MaterialApp; screens are routes managed by the Navigator.

questionsList.content: Which of the following is a normal permission in Android?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: android.permission.INTERNET is a normal permission granted automatically at install time. CAMERA, SEND_SMS and ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION are dangerous (runtime) permissions. Flutter (Module 8): http requests need INTERNET in the main AndroidManifest.xml for release builds (the Flutter template adds it only to the debug/profile manifests).

questionsList.content: List a is defined as follows: a = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] Select 2 statements that remove the middle element 3 from a so that it equals [1, 2, 4, 5]:
questionsList.explanation: Correct: del a[2] (remove by index) and a.remove(3) (remove the first element equal to 3) both give [1, 2, 4, 5]. a[2:2] = [] removes nothing, and a[2] = [] replaces 3 with an empty list. Python — outside the Flutter syllabus. Dart (Module 2 – Collections): a.removeAt(2); or a.remove(3);

questionsList.content: How do you handle intents in an IntentService?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: @Override protected void onHandleIntent(Intent intent) — called on the worker thread for each queued intent. You should not override onStartCommand() in an IntentService, and onCreate()/onDestroy() take no Intent. Flutter: there is no IntentService; use an async function/queue or an Isolate (Module 3).

questionsList.content: Which of the following correctly describes the purpose of the onProgressUpdate() method in an AsyncTask?

answersList.content: To perform long-running operations in the background
To publish progress updates to the UI thread
To initialize the task before execution
To handle the results of the background computation

questionsList.explanation: Correct: onProgressUpdate() publishes progress updates on the UI thread (it is triggered by publishProgress()). doInBackground() does the long work, onPreExecute() initializes, onPostExecute() handles the result. Flutter (Module 3): yield progress values from an async* Stream and display them with a StreamBuilder.

questionsList.content: What is an Android Service used for?

answersList.content: To perform long-running operations in the background

questionsList.explanation: Correct: an Android Service performs long-running operations in the background without a UI. It does not manage UI components, and storage/network are done with other APIs (often from inside a service). Flutter (Module 3): Futures/async for I/O and Isolates for CPU tasks; persistent background jobs need workmanager or native code.

questionsList.content: Which method is called when a Service is first created through startService() or bindService()?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: onCreate() is called once when the service is first created (by startService() or bindService()), before onStartCommand()/onBind(). onStart() is deprecated, and onResume() belongs to activities. Flutter: one-time initialization goes in a service class constructor or a singleton init(), e.g. a NotificationService initialized once at app start (Module 10).

questionsList.content: Which intent type is explicitly specified by the target component's name?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: an Explicit Intent specifies the target component by name (class). Implicit intents name an action; broadcast and sticky are delivery styles. Flutter (Module 5): MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => SecondPage()) names the exact destination.

questionsList.content: Which of the following best describes the difference between explicit and implicit Intents in Android?

answersList.content: Explicit intents specify the exact activity to start, while implicit intents declare a general action to perform.
Explicit intents are used for internal app communication, while implicit intents are used for external communication.
Explicit intents require user interaction, while implicit intents do not.
Explicit intents are faster than implicit intents

questionsList.explanation: Correct: explicit intents specify the exact activity/component to start, while implicit intents declare a general action and let the system find a matching component. Explicit intents can target another app, neither requires user interaction, and speed is not the difference. Flutter (Module 5): Navigator.push to a known widget vs deep links / url_launcher for 'any app that can handle this URL'.

questionsList.content: Which of the following can Intents do in an Android application?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: All of the above — intents start Activities (startActivity), start Services (startService) and deliver broadcasts (sendBroadcast). Flutter: Navigator handles screens; plugins hide intents for services and broadcasts.

questionsList.content: How would you create a notification channel in Android 8.0 (API level 26) or higher?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: create a NotificationChannel with its constructor (id, name, importance) and register it with NotificationManager.createNotificationChannel() (API 26+). createChannel()/createNotification() do not exist, and NotificationCompat.Builder only builds notifications. Flutter (Module 10): const AndroidNotificationChannel('login_channel', 'Login alerts', importance: Importance.high) registered with createNotificationChannel() on the Android implementation of flutter_local_notifications.

questionsList.content: What is a Notification Channel?

answersList.content: A way to group notifications by type
A method to send data between activities
A UI element to display messages
A channel to communicate with external devices

questionsList.explanation: Correct: a Notification Channel is a way to group notifications by type/category so users can control them per category. It is not for passing data between activities, a UI element, or a hardware channel. Flutter (Module 10): you pass the channel id and name in AndroidNotificationDetails.

questionsList.content: Which method is used to send an ordered broadcast, allowing you to control the order in which Broadcast Receivers receive the broadcast?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: sendOrderedBroadcast(Intent, String receiverPermission) — receivers get the broadcast one at a time in android:priority order. sendBroadcast is unordered, sticky is deprecated, sendBroadcastAsUser targets a user profile. Flutter: no equivalent; process handlers sequentially in Dart if needed.

questionsList.content: What is the purpose of a BroadcastReceiver?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: a BroadcastReceiver receives and handles broadcasts; sending is done with sendBroadcast(). Flutter: a Stream listener (Module 3).

questionsList.content: Which IDE is Android app development?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: Android Studio is the official IDE for Android app development (Eclipse ADT was deprecated). Flutter (Module 1): Flutter can be developed in Android Studio (with the Flutter plugin), VS Code (Flutter & Dart extensions) or online in DartPad.

questionsList.content: Which component would you use to perform a long-running task in the background without blocking the main thread?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: a Service performs long-running background work without blocking the main thread (in practice together with a worker thread / WorkManager, because a Service's callbacks themselves run on the main thread). Activities are UI, receivers react to events, providers share data. Flutter (Module 3/12): never block the main isolate; use async I/O and Isolate.run() / compute() for heavy CPU work.

questionsList.content: Which Android component provides a visual user interface focused on a single task a user can do?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: Activities provide a visual user interface focused on a single task the user can do (one screen). Flutter (Module 4/5): a screen is a widget (usually a Scaffold) pushed as a route.

questionsList.content: Which type of contextual menu is best suited for allowing users to select multiple items in a RecyclerView and perform a bulk action?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: Contextual Action Mode (the contextual action bar) lets users select multiple items and perform a bulk action; a floating context menu acts on a single item, the options menu is global, a popup menu is anchored to one view. Flutter: implement a selection mode — onLongPress of a ListTile toggles selection and the AppBar switches to show actions (delete/share) for the selected items.

questionsList.content: What is the role of the setImageDrawable() method in ImageView?

answersList.content: To change the visible image by setting a Drawable object
To change the visible image by setting a drawable resource ID
To change the visible image by setting a URI
To change the visible image by setting a Bitmap object

questionsList.explanation: Correct: setImageDrawable(Drawable) changes the image by setting a Drawable object. setImageResource(int) uses a resource ID, setImageURI(Uri) a URI and setImageBitmap(Bitmap) a Bitmap. Flutter (Module 4): Image.asset / Image.network / Image.file / Image.memory, or Image(image: AssetImage(...)).

questionsList.content: How does a RecyclerView improve performance compared to a traditional ListView?

answersList.content: By eliminating the need for an adapter

questionsList.explanation: Correct: RecyclerView reuses (recycles) item views/ViewHolders that scroll off-screen instead of inflating new ones, and enforces the ViewHolder pattern. It still needs an adapter and does not sort or add swipe-to-delete automatically. Flutter (Module 4/12): ListView.builder builds only the visible items lazily; extract item widgets, use const and ValueKey for best performance.

questionsList.content: Which layout manager allows a RecyclerView to display items in a grid format? Choose 2 correct answers.
questionsList.explanation: Correct: GridLayoutManager and StaggeredGridLayoutManager display items in a grid; LinearLayoutManager is a list and StackLayoutManager is not built in. Flutter (Module 6 – Responsive GridView): GridView.count(crossAxisCount: width < 600 ? 2 : 4, children: ...).

questionsList.content: To display pictures in a RecyclerView, which component is essential in your adapter's onBindViewHolder method?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: an ImageView in the item layout, filled in onBindViewHolder() (often with Glide/Picasso). TextView, EditText and CheckBox do not show pictures. Flutter (Module 4): return a ListTile with leading: Image.network(posterUrl) or CircleAvatar(backgroundImage: NetworkImage(url)) from itemBuilder.

questionsList.content: Which permissions need to be added to the AndroidManifest.xml for Google Maps to work?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: android.permission.INTERNET — the Maps SDK must download map tiles (you also add the API key meta-data; location permissions are needed only to show the user's location). Bluetooth, camera and contacts are unrelated. Flutter: google_maps_flutter needs INTERNET and the com.google.android.geo.API_KEY meta-data in AndroidManifest.xml.

questionsList.content: Which permission allows an Android application to write to external storage?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (legacy; since Android 10/11 scoped storage limits it — apps write to their own external folders or use MediaStore without it). READ_ is for reading only. Flutter (Module 9): prefer path_provider directories (no permission needed); getExternalStorageDirectory() returns app-specific external storage on Android.

questionsList.content: Which permissions are required to access the phone's location for use with Google Maps?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION or ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION (approximate vs precise) — at least one is required to access the device location on the map. Internet, Wi-Fi state, storage and network-state permissions do not give location. Flutter: declare them in AndroidManifest.xml, request at runtime (geolocator / permission_handler), then GoogleMap(myLocationEnabled: true).

questionsList.content: What does the OnMapReadyCallback interface do?

answersList.content: Loads the Google Map API key.
Notifies when the map is ready to be used.
Adds the map fragment to the layout.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: OnMapReadyCallback notifies you (via onMapReady) when the GoogleMap object is ready to be used. It does not initialize Play services, load the API key or add the fragment. Flutter: GoogleMap(onMapCreated: (controller) {...}).

questionsList.content: To insert a record into a SQLite database, which class do you use to compile the SQL query?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: SQLiteDatabase — it compiles and executes SQL (insert(), execSQL(), compileStatement()). ContentValues only holds column values, Cursor reads results, SQLiteOpenHelper manages creation and versioning. Flutter (Module 9): db.insert('todos', {'title': title, 'isDone': 0}) or db.rawInsert('INSERT INTO ...', [args]).

questionsList.content: Why is it generally recommended to use transactions when performing multiple database operations?

answersList.content: Transactions ensure atomicity; either all operations succeed, or none do.
Transactions are required by Android's SQLite implementation.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: transactions ensure atomicity — either all operations succeed or none are applied (rollback). They also often speed up bulk writes, but atomicity is the main reason; they are not mandatory. Flutter (sqflite): await db.transaction((txn) async { await txn.insert(...); await txn.update(...); }); or db.batch() for bulk operations.

questionsList.content: Which method is used for storing key-value pairs in Android?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: Shared Preferences stores key–value pairs. Internal/external storage store files, Room stores tables. Flutter (Module 9): shared_preferences — 'Key-value → SharedPreferences'.

questionsList.content: In class SQLiteOpenHelper class, there are 2 methods we should usually override. What are they?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: onCreate(SQLiteDatabase) (create the tables the first time) and onUpgrade(db, oldVersion, newVersion) (migrate when the version number increases). Note: options 1 and 5 are duplicates in this copy. Flutter (Module 9): openDatabase(path, version: 2, onCreate: (db, v) {...}, onUpgrade: (db, oldV, newV) {...}).

questionsList.content: Why might MVP be preferred over MVC in Android development?

answersList.content: MVP allows for easier unit testing by decoupling the View and the Model through the Presenter
MVP is officially recommended by Google
MVP supports asynchronous data loading natively
MVP is simpler and requires less code

questionsList.explanation: Correct: MVP decouples the View from the Model through the Presenter (the View is an interface), so presentation logic can be unit-tested without Android UI. Google does not officially recommend MVP (its guide recommends a ViewModel/UDF architecture), it has no native async loading, and it usually needs more code. Flutter (Module 11): the UI → Provider → Repository separation enables unit tests of logic and mocked repositories.

questionsList.content: Consider the following code. What is its purpose within an MVC architecture? public class LoginController { private LoginView view; private LoginModel model; public LoginController(LoginView view, LoginModel model) { this.view = view; this.model = model; } public void performLogin(String username, String password) { if (model.isValidUser(username, password)) { view.showLoginSuccess(); } else { view.showLoginError(); } } }

answersList.content: The Controller handles user input and updates the View based on the Model's data
The Controller directly updates the Model
The View handles the business logic
The Model updates the View directly

questionsList.explanation: Correct: the Controller handles user input (performLogin), checks the data through the Model (isValidUser) and updates the View (showLoginSuccess / showLoginError). Here the Controller only reads the Model, the View holds no business logic, and the Model does not touch the View. Flutter (Module 10): an AuthService/controller validates credentials and the screen reacts (navigate to Home or show a SnackBar 'Invalid credentials').

questionsList.content: What class in Android acts similarly to a Controller in the MVC pattern?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: in classic Android MVC the Activity (or Fragment) acts as the Controller — it receives input and updates the views. ViewModel belongs to MVVM; services and receivers are not controllers. Flutter (Module 5): the State object or a ChangeNotifier / Provider plays the controller role.

questionsList.content: What is the difference between @Path and @Query annotations in Retrofit?

answersList.content: @Path is used to insert values into the URL path, while @Query is used to add parameters to the URL's query string.
@Path encrypts data before sending, whereas @Query sends data in plain text.
@Path is used for POST requests, and @Query is used for GET requests.
@Path and @Query serve the same purpose and can be used interchangeably.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: @Path inserts values into the URL path ({placeholder}, e.g. /users/{id}), while @Query adds parameters to the query string (?key=value). Neither encrypts data, both work with any HTTP method, and they are not interchangeable. Flutter (Module 8): path values via string interpolation ('/users/$id'), query values via Uri queryParameters.

questionsList.content: What annotation is used in Retrofit to denote a JSON body in a POST request?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: @Body — Retrofit serializes the object with the converter (e.g. Gson) and sends it as the request body, typically JSON. @PostBody, @Json and @RequestBody are not Retrofit annotations. Flutter (Module 8 – Demo 8.3): http.post(url, headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json; charset=UTF-8'}, body: json.encode({...})); success is statusCode 201.

questionsList.content: Which method is used to create a Notification Channel? NotificationChannel channel = new NotificationChannel(channelId, name, importance);
questionsList.explanation: Correct: notificationManager.createNotificationChannel(channel); the other method names do not exist. Flutter (Module 10): androidImplementation.createNotificationChannel(channel) in flutter_local_notifications.

questionsList.content: What is Shared Preferences used for in Android development?

answersList.content: To store private primitive data in key-value pairs
To send data over the network

questionsList.explanation: Correct: Shared Preferences store private primitive data (boolean, int, float, long, String, Set<String>) in key–value pairs — not large datasets, SQLite management or networking. questionsList.content: Which changes are made when you add a second Activity to your app by choosing File > New > Activity and an Activity template?

questionsList.content: What are the advantages of using a Room database?

questionsList.content: In Android, what is the main thread also known as?

questionsList.content: Which of the following are examples of Android app components?

questionsList.content: Which folder is for XML files that contain strings, integers, and colors?

questionsList.content: When a button is clicked, which listener can you use?

questionsList.content: Which of the following should be used to save the unsaved data and release resources being used by an Android application?

questionsList.content: Which Intent action do you use to take a picture with a camera app?

questionsList.content: Which of the following are examples of Android app components?

questionsList.content: Which of the following are reasons for using a content provider in an app?

questionsList.content: What is the primary difference between a Bound Service and a Started Service (unbound) in Android?

answersList.content: Bound Services have a user interface, while Started Services don't.
Bound Services can't run in the background, while Started Services can.
Bound Services can be bound to by multiple clients, while Started Services can't.

questionsList.content: What is the difference between themes and styles?

Styles cannot inherit from other styles, but themes can inherit from other themes.

questionsList.content: What is the primary purpose of a Content Provider in Android?

questionsList.content: When establishing a connection between a client and a server using sockets, what is the purpose of the accept() method in server-side socket programming?

A device for connecting multiple Ethernet cables

questionsList.content: Which tab allows you to switch between Design and Text view in Android Studio Layout Editor?

questionsList.content: Why might you choose to use setOnTouchListener() instead of a more specific listener like setOnClickListener()?

questionsList.content: Considering the dynamic way to add Fragments to an Activity, which of the following scenarios correctly outlines the process and potential pitfalls of dynamically managing Fragments within an Activity's lifecycle?

questionsList.content: Evaluate the effectiveness of using Services for background tasks compared to Activities

questionsList.content: What are the key differences between a Floating Context Menu and Contextual Action Mode?

questionsList.content: What is the purpose of a RecyclerView in Android development?

questionsList.content: Which of the following is a key difference between the MVC and MVP architectural patterns?
