AsyncTask is deprecated since API 30. Flutter (Module 2/3/8): async/await + FutureBuilder handle 'run in the background, then update the UI' without threads.

questionsList.content: Which of the following methods is used to get result when a picture is taken?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: onActivityResult(requestCode, resultCode, data) receives the camera result (today the Activity Result API callback). onCreate/onResume are lifecycle methods. Flutter: the awaited Future of ImagePicker().pickImage(...) returns the XFile directly.

questionsList.content: Which permission do you need to declare for an HTTP connection in AndroidManifest.xml file?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: INTERNET (android.permission.INTERNET); the other names do not exist. Flutter (Module 8): required for http package calls in release builds.

questionsList.content: Which type of layout is most appropriate for aligning child View controls in relation to the parent layout?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: RelativeLayout positions child views relative to the parent or siblings (alignParentTop, centerInParent...); AbsoluteLayout is deprecated and LinearLayout only stacks. (ConstraintLayout is the modern choice.) Flutter (Module 5/6): Stack + Align / Positioned for parent-relative placement.

questionsList.content: Which of the following is the best correct statement for catching exception of the following statement: Intent intent = new Intent (MainActivity.this, DestActivity.class);
questionsList.explanation: Correct (key): NullPointerException. [CHECK] Creating an Intent normally throws nothing; startActivity() throws ActivityNotFoundException if DestActivity is not declared in the manifest — 'NotFoundActivity' in the options is not a real class (possibly a garbled ActivityNotFoundException). Use the community key with caution. Flutter: pushing an undefined named route throws a FlutterError unless onGenerateRoute / onUnknownRoute handles it (Module 5).

questionsList.content: Does android application need to be certificated in order to deploy to Android market?

answersList.content: Yes, Android uses this certificate to identify the author of an app.
No, Android will identity author of an app through Google account.
Yes, this certificate include Google account of author.
No, certificate is not required for the author of an app.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: Yes — every APK/AAB must be digitally signed with a certificate, and Android uses it to identify the author and verify that updates come from the same developer. The certificate does not contain a Google account. Flutter (Module 12 – App signing): create a keystore, reference it in android/key.properties and build.gradle, then run flutter build appbundle --release.

questionsList.content: What is the difference between the onPause() method and the onSaveInstanceState() method?

answersList.content: the onSaveInstanceState() method is not fired when an activity is being unloaded from the stack (e.g. when the user presses the Back button)
onPause() method is always fired whenever an activity is killed or pushed into the background
onSaveInstanceState() method is always fired whenever an activity is killed or pushed into the background

questionsList.explanation: [KEY CORRECTED] The original key marked only option 1. Both of the first two statements describe the difference: onSaveInstanceState() is NOT fired when an activity is being unloaded from the stack (e.g. the user presses Back), because there is no state to restore, while onPause() is ALWAYS fired whenever an activity is killed or pushed into the background. Option 3 is false, so 'All of the others' is false. If your exam accepts only one answer, the community key was option 1. Flutter: State.dispose() runs whenever a screen is removed; use RestorationMixin for state that must survive process death.

questionsList.content: The Context class's method is used to call for creating files under the application data directory. What is its name?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: openFileOutput(name, mode) on Context creates/opens a private file in the application's internal data directory and returns a FileOutputStream; openFile() and createFile() are not Context methods. Flutter (Module 9): final dir = await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory(); final file = File('${dir.path}/notes.json'); await file.writeAsString(jsonString);

questionsList.content: Which of the following is CORRECT definition of external storage?

answersList.content: Used for files without access restrictions
Upon uninstall all application related files are deleted
Secure because only the related application can access files

questionsList.explanation: Correct: external storage is used for files without access restrictions (shared / world-readable, historically), such as media. It is not secure, and files outside app-specific folders are not deleted on uninstall — those properties describe internal storage. Flutter (Module 9): prefer getApplicationDocumentsDirectory() (private) for app data.

questionsList.content: For reading the contacts from the Contacts via ContentProvider, which permission will you set in the AndroidManifest.xml file?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: READ_CONTACTS (a dangerous permission that also needs a runtime request); GET_CONTACTS and CONTACTS_ACCESS do not exist. Flutter: the flutter_contacts package (FlutterContacts.requestPermission(), FlutterContacts.getContacts()) still needs READ_CONTACTS in the manifest.

questionsList.content: Which statement is TRUE about Action Bar?

answersList.content: Replaces the traditional title bar for older versions of Android.
Action items are displayed on the right of the Action Bar. They are created just like options menu items.
Title bar for older versions of Android.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: action items are displayed on the right side of the Action Bar and are created just like options menu items (menu XML with app:showAsAction). The Action Bar replaces the title bar on newer versions, not older ones. Flutter (Module 4): AppBar(actions: [IconButton(icon: const Icon(Icons.search), onPressed: ...)]) puts actions on the right; PopupMenuButton for overflow.

questionsList.content: Which of the following view object is used in a video application?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: VideoView plays video files or streams. WebView shows web pages, and SurfaceView is a low-level drawing surface. Flutter: the video_player package (VideoPlayerController.networkUrl(...) + VideoPlayer widget); chewie adds playback controls.

questionsList.content: Which one of the following describes for the following sentence? Intent i = new Intent(MainActivity.this, TargetActivity.class); startActivity(i);

answersList.content: TargetActivity is the top of the stack activity, and start MainActivity
MainActivity transmits data to TargerActivity, and start TargetActivity
Create an instance of the TargerActivity, and start TargetActivity
Create an instance of the MainActivity, and start MainActivity

questionsList.explanation: Correct: the code creates an explicit Intent for TargetActivity and starts it (a new TargetActivity instance is placed on top of the back stack). No extras are passed, and MainActivity is the caller, not the target. Flutter (Module 5): Navigator.push(context, MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => const TargetScreen()));

questionsList.content: Which permissions do you need to declare for sending and receiving SMS messages in AndroidManifest.xml file?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: SEND_SMS and RECEIVE_SMS (dangerous permissions; Google Play also restricts SMS permissions). The other names do not exist. Flutter: url_launcher with an 'sms:' URI opens the SMS app without these permissions; sending silently needs native code / plugins plus the permissions.

questionsList.content: Which method is used to broadcast an Intent?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: sendBroadcast() broadcasts an Intent to all matching receivers; IntentBroadcast() and forwardIntent() do not exist. Flutter (Module 3): StreamController.broadcast().add(event) for in-app events.

questionsList.content: Which of the following is used to send data between 2 activities?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: a Bundle (a key–value container) carries the data, usually through intent.putExtras(bundle) / putExtra(). Toast and View are UI elements. Flutter (Module 5/8): pass objects directly through constructors (PostDetailScreen(post: post)) or the arguments of pushNamed().

questionsList.content: Which one of the following does describe how to get data from another activity through intent?

answersList.content: call getIntent() method, then getBundle() method
call getIntent() method, then getExtras() method
call getActivity() method, then getPara() method
call getActivity () method, then getData() method

questionsList.explanation: Correct: call getIntent() and then getExtras(), which returns the Bundle of extras (then read values such as getString(key)). getBundle(), getActivity(), getPara() and getData() (which returns the data URI) are not the way to read extras. Flutter (Module 5): ModalRoute.of(context)!.settings.arguments, or the widget's constructor fields.

questionsList.content: Which levels does user interact with your UI?

answersList.content: The activity level and the view level.
The activity level and layout level.
The UI activity level and the view level.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: users interact with the UI at the activity level (the screen/window: back, menus, focus) and at the view level (individual views such as buttons and text fields). Flutter (Module 4): screen level = route / Scaffold, view level = individual widgets.

questionsList.content: Which features does a fragment same as an activity?

answersList.content: They have a lifecycle that includes multiple of callback methods.
These instances are administered by the Android OS.
A device screen can contain multiple instances of them.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: like an Activity, a Fragment has a lifecycle with multiple callback methods. Fragments are managed by the host's FragmentManager (not directly by the OS), and only fragments can appear as several instances on one screen. Flutter: the State of a StatefulWidget also has lifecycle callbacks (initState, didUpdateWidget, dispose).

questionsList.content: Which of the following methods are called when the screen changes orientation from portrait to landscape in Android?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: on rotation the Activity is recreated: onPause → onSaveInstanceState → onStop → onDestroy → onCreate → onStart → onRestoreInstanceState → onResume. Option 4 is the only one whose methods are all actually called (onRestart and onActivityResult are not). Flutter (Module 6): the Flutter MainActivity is not recreated (configChanges in the manifest); widgets just rebuild, and OrientationBuilder / MediaQuery give the new orientation.

questionsList.content: Which of the following statement about PhoneGap is FALSE?

answersList.content: Use Java to write your code
Take advantage of HTML5 and CSS3

questionsList.explanation: Correct (the FALSE statement): 'Use Java to write your code' — PhoneGap/Cordova apps are written with HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript running in a WebView, can access native features through plugins and can be deployed to multiple platforms. Outside the Flutter syllabus. Flutter (Module 1 – Flutter vs Others): Flutter uses Dart and its own rendering engine instead of a WebView, while React Native uses JavaScript with bridges to native.

questionsList.content: Which of the following statement about function of class NotificationCompat.Builder is FALSE?
questionsList.explanation: Correct (the FALSE statement): setContentView(View view) — NotificationCompat.Builder has no such method (custom layouts use setCustomContentView(RemoteViews)); setContentIntent(), setSmallIcon() and setContentText() are real Builder methods. Flutter (Module 10): AndroidNotificationDetails(channelId, channelName, icon: ..., importance: ...) + show(id, title, body, details, payload: ...).

questionsList.content: Which one of the following does describe the way in which color can be applied to an element on a web page?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: in HTML/CSS a color can be written as a hex value (#FF0000) or a color name (red) (rgb()/hsl() also exist); CMYK is for print, not web pages. Flutter (Module 4): Color(0xFFFF0000) (ARGB hex) or named constants such as Colors.red.

questionsList.content: What will happen when setting the choice mode on a ListView object to CHOICE_MODE_SINGLE?

answersList.content: Make the ListView track only "selected" item.
Add a RadioButton to each item.
Add a Checkbox to each item.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: CHOICE_MODE_SINGLE makes the ListView track only one 'selected/checked' item at a time (with a choice-mode item layout it shows a radio-style check). The default is CHOICE_MODE_NONE, and it does not add RadioButtons or CheckBoxes by itself. Flutter (Module 4): RadioListTile items with one groupValue, or a selectedIndex in state with ListTile(selected: i == selectedIndex).

questionsList.content: When you create a backup agent by extending BackupAgent, which callback methods should you implement?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: a class that extends BackupAgent must implement onBackup() and onRestore(). Flutter: Android Auto Backup also backs up the SharedPreferences and app files of a Flutter app by default (controlled by android:allowBackup in the manifest).

questionsList.content: If I send a broadcast with implicit intent, and there is no maching intent-filter. What happen does user get?

answersList.content: It will throw run time exception - BroadcastReceiverNotFoundException, and crashes if it properly
Nothing will happen, somehow it launches target component
Nothing will happen , but it will not launch any receiver

questionsList.explanation: Correct: nothing happens — sending a broadcast that no receiver matches is not an error: no receiver runs and there is no compile error, exception or crash (unlike startActivity() with no match, which throws ActivityNotFoundException). Flutter: adding an event to a broadcast StreamController with no listeners simply drops it (Module 3).

questionsList.content: Which layout manager do you use android:layout_toRightOf with?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: android:layout_toRightOf is a RelativeLayout parameter (position a view to the right of a sibling). Flutter: Row(children: [a, b]) places b to the right of a.

questionsList.content: What is the name of the class which is inherited to create a user interface screen?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: Activity — you subclass Activity (AppCompatActivity) to create a user-interface screen; View/ViewGroup are building blocks inside it and Canvas is for drawing. Flutter (Module 4/5): you create a screen by extending StatelessWidget or StatefulWidget and returning a Scaffold.

questionsList.content: In HTML5, which method is used to get the current location of a user?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(successCallback, errorCallback) from the HTML5 Geolocation API; getPosition()/getUserPosition() do not exist. Outside the Flutter syllabus. Flutter: geolocator — final pos = await Geolocator.getCurrentPosition();

questionsList.content: Which of the following statement is TRUE about PhoneGap?

answersList.content: NodeJS is a mandatory dependency for PhoneGap development.
The Cordova CLI is built on top of the PhoneGap CLI.
PhoneGap framework is a cloud-based service built on top of the PhoneGap Build.
A PhoneGap application may only use PHP and JavaScript.

questionsList.explanation: Correct (key): option 3. [CHECK] The option text is reversed: in reality PhoneGap Build is a cloud-based service built on top of the PhoneGap framework (and the PhoneGap CLI is built on top of the Cordova CLI). Choose option 3 as the intended answer. Outside the Flutter syllabus. Flutter (Module 1): Flutter compiles Dart to native ARM code with its own engine, unlike PhoneGap's WebView approach.

questionsList.content: How does a <fragment> tag specify which fragment to use?
questionsList.explanation: Correct (key): the 'class' attribute — <fragment class="com.example.MyFragment" .../> (android:name works the same way). android:id only identifies the fragment, and android:fragment is not a valid attribute here. Flutter: you simply instantiate the widget class you want in the tree, e.g. child: const MovieDetailPage().

questionsList.content: Which of the following is CORRECT definition of Toast?

answersList.content: Show a short message and auto dismiss after very short time.
Show a complicate message, include image, button, choice...
Show a message and wait for user respond.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: a Toast shows a short message and dismisses itself automatically after a short time; it cannot hold complex content or wait for the user's response (that is a dialog). Flutter (Module 7/8/10 demos): SnackBar via ScaffoldMessenger (auto-dismisses, optional action).

questionsList.content: What is a back stack used for?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: the back stack is used for both Activities (the task back stack) and Fragments (the FragmentManager back stack via addToBackStack()). Flutter (Module 5): the Navigator's stack of routes — push adds a page, pop removes it.

questionsList.content: What does the part <authority> in Content URI format describe?

answersList.content: specify the unique name of content provider
specify the path to data which is provided
specify the particular record which user requires

questionsList.explanation: Correct: <authority> is the unique (symbolic) name of the content provider, usually the app package + '.provider'. The path specifies which data/table and the ID a particular record. Flutter: in Dart's Uri the authority corresponds to the host component.

questionsList.content: Which of the following is correctly describes when you call method "onDestroy()"?

answersList.content: Called as part of the activity lifecycle when an activity is going into the background, but has not (yet) been killed
Called when you are no longer visible to the user
Called when the activity is finishing
Called after your activity has been stopped, prior to it being started again

questionsList.explanation: Correct: onDestroy() is called when the activity is finishing (finish() or Back) or is being destroyed by the system (e.g. during a configuration change). Option 1 describes onPause(), option 2 onStop(), option 4 onRestart(). Flutter (Module 5/8): State.dispose() — release resources there, e.g. TextEditingController.dispose() in Demo 8.3.

questionsList.content: How is Android OS divided?

answersList.content: five section in four main layers.
four section in four main layers.
four section in five main layers.

questionsList.explanation: Correct (key): the Android OS stack is commonly described as five sections in four main layers (Linux kernel; libraries + Android runtime; application framework; applications). Flutter (Module 1): Flutter's own architecture has three layers — Framework, Engine, Embedder.

questionsList.content: How do you add action items to the Action Bar?

answersList.content: Simply handle the onCreateOptionsMenu() and onOptionsItemSelected() events.
Simply handle the onCreateItems() and onOptionsItemSelected() events.
Simply handle the onCreateActionBar() and onActionBarItemSelected() events.
Simply handle the onMenuCreate() and onItemSelected() events.

questionsList.explanation: Correct: override onCreateOptionsMenu() to inflate the menu items (showAsAction puts them in the Action Bar) and onOptionsItemSelected() to handle clicks. The other callback names do not exist. Flutter (Module 4): AppBar(actions: [...]) with onPressed / onSelected callbacks.

questionsList.content: In the Android Licensing Service, what does LVL stand for?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: LVL = License Verification Library — it checks the user's license with the Google Play licensing service. Outside the Flutter syllabus (the modern equivalent is the Play Integrity API).

questionsList.content: Which of the following application should be installed on Internal Storage?
questionsList.explanation: [KEY CORRECTED] The original key marked only 'App widgets' (votes were split 7/14). Android docs say apps that use Services, Alarm services, App Widgets, Input Method Engines, Live Wallpapers, Account Managers, Sync Adapters, Device Administrators or BOOT_COMPLETED receivers should NOT be installed on external storage, because those features stop working when the storage is unmounted. So both 'Alarm service' and 'App widgets' are correct; if only one choice is allowed, the community key was 'App widgets'. Flutter: controlled the same way with android:installLocation in AndroidManifest.xml (default: internal only).

questionsList.content: Which of the following is the advantage of SQLiteOpenHelper class that makes it preferred over SQLiteDatabase class when manipulating database?

answersList.content: It can read and write a database
It can initialize tables of a newly-created database while SQLiteDatabase can not
It caches database instances and closes them when they are no longer needed
It has better performance than SQLiteDatabase

questionsList.explanation: Correct (key): SQLiteOpenHelper can initialize the tables of a newly created database (onCreate) and handle upgrades with versioning (onUpgrade), which SQLiteDatabase alone does not provide. It does cache the opened database instance, but it does not close it automatically, and it is not inherently faster. Flutter (Module 9): openDatabase(path, version: ..., onCreate: ..., onUpgrade: ...) gives the same create/upgrade hooks.

questionsList.content: Which of the following statements about PhoneGap is FALSE?

answersList.content: It only the purpose of PhoneGap to distribute the web application to application store.
It is an open source development framework for building cross platform mobile apps.
It allows you to package your mobile web application code and resources into a binary app and then distribute it to mobile devices.

questionsList.explanation: Correct (the FALSE statement): 'The only purpose of PhoneGap is to distribute the web application to the application store' — PhoneGap is an open-source framework for building cross-platform mobile apps with web technologies and packaging them as native binaries for distribution. Outside the Flutter syllabus. Flutter (Module 1): Flutter is also cross-platform from a single codebase, but renders a natively compiled UI.

questionsList.content: Which of the following attribute of AndroidManifest.xml is NOT a must have attribute when publishing an application on Android Market?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: android:versionAndroid does not exist; android:versionCode (an integer that must increase with every release) and android:versionName (the displayed version string) are required for publishing. Flutter (Module 12): set version: 1.0.0+1 in pubspec.yaml → versionName 1.0.0, versionCode 1 (read by android/app/build.gradle); increase the build number for every release.

questionsList.content: Which kind of notification is NOT supported in android?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: 'Permission notification' is not a notification kind; Toast and Dialog notifications (and status bar notifications) are supported. Flutter: SnackBar, AlertDialog and local notifications (Module 10).

questionsList.content: Which type of button control is available on the Android platform?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: ImageButton (a button that shows an image) is a standard Android control; DrawableButton and RoundCornerButton do not exist. Flutter (Module 4): IconButton(icon: const Icon(Icons.favorite), onPressed: ...) or an ElevatedButton with a rounded shape.

questionsList.content: Which of the following is NOT the PhoneGap Events?
questionsList.explanation: Correct: 'forward' is not a PhoneGap/Cordova event; real events include deviceready, pause, resume, backbutton, menubutton, searchbutton, batterystatus and online/offline. Outside the Flutter syllabus. Flutter: lifecycle events via WidgetsBindingObserver (AppLifecycleState), the back button via PopScope, battery via battery_plus.
